The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 24.09.2024.

2. The Brief facts of the case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 24.09.2024 at about 03.00 p.m., petitioner was crossing the Bannerghatta - Gigani main road carefully and cautiously by following all traffic rules and regulations, near Venkateshwara Polytechnic College, at that time one Mahendra Goods bearing Reg. No. KA-51-AD-7240 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life came at high speed in a zig-zag manner and dashed against petitioner.
Due to forced impact, petitioner and rider fell down from the scooter and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, she was shifted to Parijatha Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Forties Hospital and again shifted to Medax Hospital, wherein she was treated as inpatient and spent more than Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance,
food, transport and other charges.

The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident she was heal and healthy and aged about 16 years, the petitioner was a 1st year Diploma student and also part time tailoring work at home and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost her future income.
Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notice, respondent No.1 remained absent.
Hence, placed exparte.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition.
Further this respondent admits the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further this respondent submitted that, the driver of the insured vehicle has no valid and effective driving license to drive the Mahindra Goods Vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-51-AD-7240 at the time of accident and the owner of the vehicle knowingly entrusted the vehicle to a person who was not having valid and effective driving license and violated the policy conditions.
Further, the offending Mahindra Goods vehicle has no permit to ply the vehicle in the place of accident.
Further, this respondent denies the involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident and there was an inordinate delay in lodging the complaint.
Further this respondent denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, she is the victim of the motor vehicle accident caused by the driver of Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-51- AD-7240 at about 03.00 p.m., near Venkateshwara Polytechnic college, Bannerghatta, Bangalore and sustained injuries as pleaded in the petition?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or Award?

5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.14 and also examined MRO at Medax Hospital as P.W.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.15 to Ex.P.18 and closed his side.
On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of the respondents.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the materials placed on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under; Issue No.1: In the affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:

:REASONS:
8. ISSUE No.1:

The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
9. The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.
He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 14.
Ex.P.1 is the FIR,

3 Ex.P.2 is the Complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the IMV Report, Ex.P.5 is the Wound certificate, Ex.P.6 is the Notice U/s 133 of M. V. Act, Ex.P.7 is the Reply Notice, Ex.P.8 is the Charge-sheet, Ex.P.9 is the outpatient record, Ex.P.10 is the Discharge summary, Ex.P.11 and Ex.P.12 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card of petitioner and guardian of petitioner, Ex.P.13 is the Medical Bills and Ex.P.14 is the Prescriptions.

10. On going through the materials, it could be seen that on 24.09.2024 at about 03.00 p.m.,
petitioner was crossing the Bannerghatta - Gigani main road carefully and cautiously by following all traffic rules and regulations, near Venkateshwara Polytechnic College, at that time one Mahendra Goods bearing Reg. No. KA-51-AD-7240 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life came at high speed in a zig-zag manner and dashed against petitioner.
Due to forced impact, petitioner and rider fell down from the scooter and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, she was shifted to Parijatha Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Forties Hospital and again shifted to Medax Hospital, wherein she was treated as inpatient.
Accordingly, the Bannerghatta Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.253/2024.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 281 and 125(a) of BNS.
11.
The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the Bannerghatta Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P.2.
On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No.253/2024.
The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P.1 along with complaint.
12. Ex.P.1 to 8 are the only documents, which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving by the driver of offending vehicle.

The Ex.P.3 (spot panchanama), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.8, Charge-Sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle U/s. 281 and 125(a) of BNS.
The Ex.P.4 i.e., certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.

13. It must be noted that, in the cross- examination of PW.1, it is suggested by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 that, petitioner herself fell and sustained injuries, but on perusal of medical records at Ex.P.9 as well as Discharge summary, it reveals that, petitioner sustained the injuries due to RTA.
In support of said documents, petitioner also relied upon the FIR as well as Police Documents.
As stated above, in this case though Insurance Company has taken defence that, the accident has not happened due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the insured vehicle.
However, in order to support their claim they have not adduced any evidence.

On the other hand,
the first respondent has not adduced any evidence before the Court.
Besides, the respondents have neither adduced any evidence not produced any documents before this Court.

Thus, these facts,
make it clear that, except allegations, the respondent No.2 has not made any efforts to show that,
accident had happened because of the fault of the petitioner.

sentences.text: It is further contended that, petitioner has filed complaint against the driver of the offending vehicle on 25.09.2024 i.e., after 01 day from the date of incident.
This tribunal opine that, treatment of the victim is given priority over lodging of FIR and delay of lodging of FIR cannot be ground to deny the justice to the claimants.

This view of this tribunal receives support from decisions of Hon'ble Apex Court as well as High Court which are reported in, 2022 ACJ 2482 between United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Sahanaz Bibi and others, 2022 ACJ 170 between Venkatesha K. N Vs.
Thipregowda and others and 2011 ACJ 2350 between Bangalore Metropolitan Transport Corporation Vs. Pullaiah .

sentences.text: Moreover, as per Ex.P.5 i.e., Wound Certificate issued by the Medax Hospital, shows that petitioner admitted to the hospital with history of RTA on 24.09.2024 itself i.e., at 02.30 PM.
So, on going through the above documents goes to show that, accident taken place on 24.09.2024 itself.
15. As stated above, respondents have not produced any evidence before this court to show that, the accident is not caused due to the driver of the offending vehicle.
Thus, the above discussion makes it clear that, except barred allegations, the respondent No.2 has not made any efforts to show that, the accident had happened because of the fault of the petitioner.
It is well settled that, in Motor vehicle accident compensation cases, the strict proof of negligence is not required.

This view of this Court receives support from the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in (2009)
13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others Vs. HRTC.

sentences.text:
Thus, I opine that, these facts are sufficient to conclude that, the accident had happened because of the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Mahendra Goods bearing Reg. No. KA-51-AD-7240.
16.
The next question would be, whether the petitioner sustained injuries in the accident or not.
It must be noted that, the Ex.P.5 i.e., Wound Certificate shows that, the petitioner was admitted to Medax Hospital on 25.09.2024.
Further, Wound Certificate shows that, the injury sustained by the petitioner is grievous in nature.

Further, in the said Wound Certificate it is mentioned that,
petitioner admitted to the hospital with alleged history of RTA.
These facts are not denied by the respondent No.2.
Hence, these facts are sufficient to conclude that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.2:

The PW.1 in her evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Parijatha Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Forties Hospital and again shifted to Medax Hospital, wherein she was treated as inpatient and took treatment.

Petitioner has stated in the petition that, she is undergoing deep mental shock,
severe pain and sufferings.

18. In the petition as well as in her evidence PW.1 deposed that, after the accident she was shifted to Medax Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P.10.
Further the petitioner has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.5, wherein the doctor has opined that the injuries are grievous in nature.
19 . The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that she has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In support of her plea, she has produced 33 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.13 to the tune of Rs.1,48,777/-.

sentences.text: Further the petitioner contended that, prior to the accident she was a 1 st year Diploma student and also part time tailoring work at home and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, but in order to prove the said fact petitioner has not produced any relevant evidences.
Petitioner also examined MRO at Medax Hospital as PW.2 who depose and produced about medical documents marked at Ex.P.15 to Ex.P.18, but his evidence is formal in nature.
21. In this case the petitioner has neither adduced the evidence of doctor nor produced any disability certificate to show that she has become permanently disabled.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income or under any other heads.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.
The petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- including the medical expenses.
22. LIABILITY:

As discussed in Issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Mahendra Goods bearing Reg. No. KA-51-AD-7240 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending vehicle punishable U/s 281 and 125(a) of BNS.
From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.2 for the period from 21.05.2024 to 20.05.2025.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 24.09.2024.
Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.1 being the owner is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 insurer.
23. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand.
Accordingly, issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
24. ISSUE No.3:
In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I. M. V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 being insurer of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
